searchText: yeah, EIP-8136 & https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4558 <@106441459183423488> can we get a gloas rebased pr too similar to this? yes, I'll open something today <@412614104222531604> can we run the blob-devnet-0 network in a partial-message-only mode for a bit? it’s like that for 4 days now Why are there other non-partial-message nodes in the network then? What did you change? Maybe I'm misunderstanding the setup The goal with this change is to exercise only the partial message paths and remove the ability to fallback on full data columns. which ones? I saw some teku nodes, but I guess they just missed their slot? Are the `-2` nodes running with partial messages on or off? teku nodes aren’t online all of them running partial on you still see some nodes with the flag off ? I still see full data column traffic. I'm looking through the logs. I suspect this is due to gossiping IHAVEs Here's the bandwidth drop after we went to partial message only from the mixed state. The bandwidth savings are there, but I think it could be better. I suspect there's an issue where nodes are still gossiping full data columns with `IHAVE` even if the peer supports partial messages. Take a look at this graph that just shows avg gossipsub datacolumn bandwidth for full data columns: We see the drop, but lighthouse supernodes are still sending a fair amount of full data columns out. <@1000001410538151996> , could you take a look? My hunch is that you might still be sending `IHAVE`s to peers about your full data columns. Those peers then request them and you end up sending out full data columns. This would be consistent with the behavior we see with non-supernode lighthouse nodes increasing their full datacolumn traffic. The non-supernodes for Prysm also still see a fair amount of full datacolumn traffic. And notice it's a bit bursty. I think this is due to the "fanout" topics not properly being marked as partial message capable. Aarsh (sorry, I don't know how to tag you directly), I think there's a bug where we aren't passing in the "[Requests/SupportsPartialMessage](https://github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-pubsub/blob/5cde33c38137d80c2d7cf3c2a5152ce7e7e05f49/pubsub.go#L1617)" `TopicOpt` when we join the topic to do a fanout (a publish to a column we aren't subscribed to). Aarsh, we need to pass these topic options anytime we would join a data column sidecar topic: https://github.com/MarcoPolo/prysm/blob/e8480a86afbf850505f5e023754b7266257d3175/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L627. We currently only do that in `trySubscribeSubnets`, but that only does it for subnets we join. We don't do it for subnets we haven't joined but publish to when we are the proposer. For example, we probably need to do it [here](https://github.com/MarcoPolo/prysm/blob/e8480a86afbf850505f5e023754b7266257d3175/beacon-chain/p2p/pubsub.go#L104), and [here](https://github.com/MarcoPolo/prysm/blob/e8480a86afbf850505f5e023754b7266257d3175/beacon-chain/p2p/pubsub.go#L83), and anywhere else we call `.JoinTopic`. It might make sense to have this done by `JoinTopic` if it is datacolumn topic and we have the partial message flag set. This experiment was super helpful. Ty <@412614104222531604> let me know if i can do anything else Glamsterdam question: What's the purpose of the `slot` field in the DataColumnSidecar? cc <@833706406699073536> Spec changes for Gloas started here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5141 please review folks
